question: Which causal-discovery systems exist today, what evidence may each use (D, I, K), where do its edge directions come from, and how was it evaluated (benchmarks, reported numbers, name/column-order controls)?

schema.name: system name
schema.category: classical | continuous optimisation | pretrained / amortised | LLM-assisted discovery | agent (+ subtype) | benchmark control
schema.venue_or_arxiv: venue if seen on a primary page; otherwise arXiv id and an explicit "not on abs page" note
schema.regimes: subset of D (observational data), I (interventional data), K (declared knowledge: variable names, descriptions, LLM priors, tiers, background knowledge)
schema.order_source: where edge directions come from: data pattern, functional-form asymmetry, interventions, LLM/name knowledge, column order, learned prior
schema.hidden_confounders_supported: true / false / null (unknown or not verified)
schema.max_variables_reported: largest graph in the cited evaluation, or null
schema.best_reported: list of {benchmark, metric, value, label}; label is reported / reported (other authors) / second-hand / measured (project)
schema.controls_reported: subset of names_neutralised, names_permuted, columns_shuffled, or ["none"]
schema.other_controls: memorisation probes, architectural invariance, augmentation, etc.
schema.q_cells: questions addressed (skeleton, orientation, effects, choice of experiments, ...)
schema.code_url: public code, or null if none found
schema.last_commit_or_release: as visible (GitHub pages did not show commit dates; PyPI upload dates used)
schema.order_source_code: short code: DATA, FUNC, INT, SCORE, LEARNED, LLM, COL (* = only via a benchmark wrapper that forces undirected edges to a DAG by column index), RANDOM-ORDER, AGENT
